description: Developer-only canonical UI source catalogue. Runtime dictionaries are Lua. Keys are exact English UI source strings or explicit named-token templates.

strings.Bluetooth earbuds and headphones play so: Bluetooth earbuds and headphones play sound a little later than the picture, so lips and subtitles can run slightly ahead of the voice. This holds them back to match, for every voice. Auto uses 150 ms while Windows plays through a Bluetooth device and none otherwise; choose a value if your headset is faster or slower. The game’s own dialogue has the same Bluetooth delay and does not correct it.

strings.Let companions speak the way a real pers: Let companions speak the way a real person with their personality would: now and then a pause, a hesitation, a laugh or a sigh. Each character decides when it fits, and it stays rare; a fluent, confident speaker will hardly use it. OmniVoice can voice laughs and sighs; Pocket TTS uses only pauses in the sentence. It needs a local voice: choosing the Convai cloud voice keeps it and turns this off, and turning this on while the cloud voice is saved moves Companion voices to Pocket TTS. Off by default.
strings.Let each character mark its own feelings: Let each character mark its own feelings as it speaks, so the face changes when that part is spoken instead of being guessed from the words. Subtle by default, chosen by personality, and only where the feeling really shifts. It needs a local voice: choosing the Convai cloud voice keeps it and turns this off, and turning this on while the cloud voice is saved moves Companion voices to Pocket TTS. A reply without marks uses the usual text-based expression. On by default.
strings.Lets you talk to unnamed people the game: Lets you talk to unnamed people the game does not give a story role: gang members, NCPD officers, corporate guards, ripperdocs, shopkeepers, bartenders and passers-by. Each answers as their kind of person, does not know your story and does not remember you after you load a save, except shopkeepers you come back to. Named characters are not affected. On by default.

strings.Pocket is light and fast on your CPU and: Pocket is light and fast on your CPU and starts speaking in about 0.2 s. OmniVoice sounds better, especially on harder voices, but needs a capable GPU and the optional OmniVoice pack (without it those entries are marked and cannot be applied), and the higher tiers take longer to start speaking, about 1 to 2.5 s. The Mistral cloud voice (Voxtral) speaks in each companion’s own voice using your Mistral key, whichever provider writes the replies; it needs a key and speaks English only. Convai uses its cloud; if a choice cannot run, a simpler voice takes over and you are told once.
strings.Prepares the conversation with a charact: Prepares the conversation with a character you look at, walk up to or have just talked to, so they answer without a wait; it pauses during combat and scenes. At most two characters are kept ready at any moment, at most one new connection starts every 3 seconds and a character is released after 40 seconds unused, so a crowd never adds up.

strings.When you talk to a character right after: When you talk to a character right after the game’s own dialogue with them, they know the last few lines that were just said, including your chosen replies and phone calls with them, so their answer follows on naturally. Only lines from the last few minutes that involved that character are used, and they are not added to the character’s memory. On by default.
strings.Which provider answers your conversation: Which provider answers your conversations right now and, for Convai, which plan pays for them. Changes wait until no conversation is running.
strings.Who writes your companions’ replies. Con: Who writes your companions’ replies. Convai is the default and the recommended choice, with better quality responses. Mistral uses its free plan with your own free key (add it below; signing up needs phone verification): memory stays on this computer, and the free plan allows about one message a second and a monthly allowance. A Convai cloud voice is replaced by a local voice. Speech is recognized on this computer, so the voice key works. The change waits until no conversation is running; choose Apply.

Who writes your companions’ replies. Convai is the default and the recommended choice, with better quality responses. Mistral uses its free plan with your own free key (add it below; signing up needs phone verification): memory stays on this computer, and the free plan allows about one message a second and a monthly allowance. A Convai cloud voice is replaced by a local voice. Speech recognition for the voice key is not available yet with Mistral, so type your messages. The change waits until no conversation is running; choose Apply.

Bluetooth earbuds and headphones play sound a little later than the picture, so lips and subtitles can run slightly ahead of the voice. This holds them back to match, for every voice. Auto uses 150 ms while Windows plays through a Bluetooth device and none otherwise; choose a value if your headset is faster or slower. The game’s own dialogue has the same Bluetooth delay and does not correct it.

Let companions speak the way a real person with their personality would: now and then a pause, a hesitation, a laugh or a sigh. Each character decides when it fits, and it stays rare; a fluent, confident speaker will hardly use it. OmniVoice can voice laughs and sighs; Pocket TTS uses only pauses in the sentence. It needs a local voice: choosing the Convai cloud voice keeps it and turns this off, and turning this on while the cloud voice is saved moves Companion voices to Pocket TTS. Off by default.

Let each character mark its own feelings as it speaks, so the face changes when that part is spoken instead of being guessed from the words. Subtle by default, chosen by personality, and only where the feeling really shifts. It needs a local voice: choosing the Convai cloud voice keeps it and turns this off, and turning this on while the cloud voice is saved moves Companion voices to Pocket TTS. A reply without marks uses the usual text-based expression. On by default.

Lets you talk to unnamed people the game does not give a story role: gang members, NCPD officers, corporate guards, ripperdocs, shopkeepers, bartenders and passers-by. Each answers as their kind of person, does not know your story and does not remember you after you load a save, except shopkeepers you come back to. Named characters are not affected. On by default.

Play voiced replies from your companions.

Pocket is light and fast on your CPU and starts speaking in about 0.2 s. OmniVoice sounds better, especially on harder voices, but needs a capable GPU and the optional OmniVoice pack (without it those entries are marked and cannot be applied), and the higher tiers take longer to start speaking, about 1 to 2.5 s. The Mistral cloud voice (Voxtral) speaks in each companion’s own voice using your Mistral key, whichever provider writes the replies; it needs a key and speaks English only. Convai uses its cloud; if a choice cannot run, a simpler voice takes over and you are told once.

Prepares the conversation with a character you look at, walk up to or have just talked to, so they answer without a wait; it pauses during combat and scenes. At most two characters are kept ready at any moment, at most one new connection starts every 3 seconds and a character is released after 40 seconds unused, so a crowd never adds up.

Remember each companion’s prepared voice so summoning them again is quicker. Pocket TTS saves one small file per character (about 5 to 15 MB) in the mod’s runtime folder; OmniVoice does a short hidden warm-up at your chosen quality while a companion joins. Turn this off to save nothing on disk. The change applies without a restart.

Talk to companions in any language: each character answers in the language you use. It uses a multilingual copy of each character, so what they remember from these conversations is kept apart from your English ones; forgetting a character clears both. Pocket TTS speaks only English, so turning this on switches Companion voices to OmniVoice · Balanced when the optional OmniVoice pack is installed, or to Convai · Cloud voice otherwise; without the pack, Natural speech and Expressive emotions are turned off, because the cloud voice would read their tags aloud. nativeHandling.note: The title prefix TALK TO and exact English message currently identify this mod’s composer. Replace that ownership test with a language-independent marker before translating either. Do not identify every generic input by its translated text.

Native creation sets CHAT/Chat and fallback Enter/Esc hints. Refresh existing widgets on locale change, and translate only mod-owned Chat widgets. The current ^ENTER status filter is English-specific. Native Messages/Contacts and game SMS stay game-localized.

Immediate queued/unavailable feedback is created in redscript before Lua replies. It needs the same dictionary through a native bridge or a scoped Lua hook. J/L key textures and button codes are not translation strings.
Legacy native manager strings are inventoried for completeness; MCM is the active manager. Do not expose or revive this retired screen just to prove localization. Its F5 footer is historical.

MCM owns Apply/Revert, search placeholders and framework status such as Completed. Provider-owned schema strings can be localized here; framework strings require MCM localization. Do not match a translated Completed prefix to decide success.

Catalogue names, summaries, model records, AI replies, provider errors, and game-localized character names are not blindly translated. Translate a curated UI error at its origin; preserve arbitrary inserted content as data.
